reviewMethod: Only the explicitly listed references are approved. Previously inspected human specimens retain their original evidence timestamps; new sources have actual source-page screenshot evidence and caption/rights review. No source images are bundled.

axial-brain-mri.title: Normal axial T2-weighted MR image of the brain
axial-brain-mri.creator: Novaksean; cropped version by Mikael Häggström
axial-brain-mri.matches: Actual axial T2 brain MRI at the lateral ventricles; inspected image shows a transverse human head/brain section with both hemispheres and ventricles.
axial-brain-mri.viewLimitations: A regional transverse imaging example, not a gross section, whole-body photograph, or a matched donor for the sagittal/coronal specimens.
axial-brain-mri.linkingTerms: Ordinary Commons file-page link. The source identifies the author and CC BY-SA 4.0; no image reuse is performed.
axial-brain-mri.reproductionRights: CC BY-SA 4.0 stated on the file page; no reproduction or embedding in the app.

human-smooth-muscle.title: Uterus. Human. Progravid. H&E. — slide 66
human-smooth-muscle.source: Columbia University Department of Pathology and Cell Biology
human-smooth-muscle.creator: Columbia University Department of Pathology and Cell Biology; individual slide photographer not separately named
human-smooth-muscle.matches: The human uterine section shows a broad myometrial smooth-muscle region. The linked laboratory commentary specifically describes fascicles arranged in different planes and distinguishes the myometrium from endometrium.
human-smooth-muscle.viewLimitations: A real organ section requiring the slide viewer's zoom, not isolated idealized spindle cells. Different section planes cross smooth-muscle fascicles; the bottom glandular region is endometrium, not muscle.
human-smooth-muscle.linkingTerms: Public university slide page, ordinary outbound link. Visible footer identifies content CC BY-SA 4.0 separately from GPLv3 viewer code. No image or viewer is embedded.
human-smooth-muscle.reproductionRights: Page footer states content CC BY-SA 4.0. The slide itself credits Columbia University Department of Pathology and Cell Biology. No reproduction is performed.

verification.visualEvidence: Actual rendered slide 66 inspected: caption explicitly reads Uterus. Human. Progravid. H&E.; large pink myometrium and adjacent glandular endometrium are visible. mappings.reason: Reinspection confirms a real assembled human foot with exposed dorsal tarsal surfaces, all three cuneiforms, metatarsals and phalanges; the first toe has two phalanges. The view is oblique and the toes point down the photograph, unlike the toes-up schematic. Side is not stated by the source and is not asserted in the link.

subject.en: Foot bones, dorsal-oblique view; side unstated
subject.es: Huesos del pie, vista dorsoblicua; lado no indicado

refs.matches: Actual human foot photograph visibly shows calcaneus, talus, navicular, cuboid, three cuneiforms, metatarsals and phalanges; individual bone groups are identified on the photograph.
refs.viewLimitations: Dorsal-oblique assembly with toes downward and distal tibia attached. Source does not state side; not claimed to be the schematic's right foot.
refs.reinspection: Fresh Commons source-page screenshot inspected, including the actual bone photograph and painted labels: /tmp/replit-screenshots/commons_wikimedia_org_wiki_File_Foot_bones_-_tarsus_metatarsus_and_phalanges_yoKi.png.

mappings.reason: Three individually named human references cover skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle and smooth muscle. Skeletal is electron microscopy, cardiac is light microscopy, and smooth muscle is a zoomable human uterine section; they are not matched stains, scale or section planes.

The previously inspected human dissection depicts all four required muscles: rectus abdominis, external oblique, internal oblique and transversus abdominis. A single layered left anterolateral field is a suitable limited real example; three separate schematic panels and identical orientation are not required.

subject.en: Abdominal wall: all four muscles, one left anterolateral dissection
subject.es: Pared abdominal: los cuatro músculos, una disección anterolateral izquierda

refs.viewLimitations: One left anterolateral layered dissection rather than three sequential schematic panels; complementary real anatomy, not identical artwork.

mappings.reason: The inspected human renal-cortex photograph shows cuboidal cells with round nuclei surrounding renal-tubule lumina. It is a specifically identified human example of the epithelial type, not a claim that the original unclassified photomicrograph has established species.

subject.en: Simple cuboidal epithelium: human renal tubules
subject.es: Epitelio cúbico simple: túbulos renales humanos

refs.matches: Human renal tubules lined by cuboidal epithelial cells, with rounded nuclei and lumina, visible in the actual source-page photograph.
refs.viewLimitations: A renal-cortex field also containing a glomerulus and vessels, not an isolated idealized epithelial strip or the identical original photograph.
refs.reinspection: The public Commons source page was opened on 2026-11-07. Its actual 600x human renal-cortex photograph visibly resolves cuboidal tubular epithelium and round nuclei around tubular lumina. Caption identifies human kidney cortex. No photograph was downloaded or retained in the project.

mappings.reason: Three previously inspected human specimens cover the named anatomy together: the superior vault shows frontal/parietal bones and coronal/sagittal sutures; the posterior lambda detail shows the lambdoid junction and adjoining occipital/parietal bone; the external skull base supplies temporal-bone context. Related examples, not a matched superior/posterior pair: the posterior source is explicitly a close detail and the temporal reference is an inferior view.

refs.viewLimitations: Superior vault specimen; not a whole posterior skull view or a matched donor.
Close detail of the sagittal/lambdoid junction, not the complete posterior contour.

subject.es: Huesos temporales: contexto inferior del cráneo

mappings.reason: The previously inspected frontal human pelvis depicts the sacrum and both hip bones, including iliac, pubic, ischial and acetabular regions. The separately inspected human femur supplies the missing femoral subject.
